//: A filled-in configuration for the four roles in roles.sql.
Every string may carry a dollar-brace environment reference, filled in when
the file loads, so this file holds no secret and is safe to commit. Export
the four passwords before starting anything that reads it.
The four connections are the point. Collapse them into one and the tool still
works, but the separation it advertises then rests entirely on this library
being free of bugs -- which is a claim no library should ask you to accept.
`llm-safe-sql check` prints which separations it could prove by asking the
server, and warns about each one it could not.
//schema: Set it on every connection, even when it is `public`.
PostgreSQL's default search_path is "$user", public, which resolves per
role -- and this library recommends giving plan and apply different roles.
Leave it unset and the planner can measure public.orders while the apply
writes llm_apply.orders, with no error anywhere. Pinned here, `check`
asserts what the server actually resolved rather than trusting the setting.
//connection: The dry run. Really executes, always rolls back. Never commits.
//readConnection: What the model reads through. PostgreSQL refuses writes on it.
//applyConnection: The only credential here that commits. Different process, different role.
//storeConnection: Plans and audit records. No privilege on business tables.

policy.//allow: Default-deny. Mirror this list in the GRANTs in roles.sql.
//impact: Required before any write to a table can be planned at all. Without it the
engine refuses with IMPACT_UNDECLARED, on purpose: strip these sentences
out and the confirmation card becomes a list of column names and old/new
values, which the person approving cannot judge. They will click yes
Write the consequence, not the mechanism. Not 'sets the status column' --
say what happens in the world when it changes.

impact.orders: Marking an order shipped emails the customer and starts the 14-day return window. It cannot be taken back by editing the row again.

policy.//denyIdentifiers: Never appears in any statement, read or write, mapped to the reason a human is told.

denyIdentifiers.password_hash: Credentials are never read through an assistant.
denyIdentifiers.api_token: A credential you can read is a credential you have leaked.

denyWriteColumns.orders.ref: The order reference is printed on the customer's invoice and is quoted in support tickets.

//autoColumns: Columns the database maintains by itself, per table. They are dropped from
the diff -- otherwise every card would show an updated_at change nobody
decided -- and assigning one is refused outright.
Get this list from `llm-safe-sql check`, which reports the triggers and
defaults it found, rather than from memory.
